sections.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in 2D Euler Equations
sections.abstract: The authors establish an integral criterion on a finite nondecreasing envelope of vorticity Lᵖ norms that separates uniqueness from nonuniqueness for a specified class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim a sharp two-sided dichotomy, including uniqueness even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions on the divergent-integral side. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations and 0 influential citations at snapshot time; no independent expert discussion surfaced, so ranking reflects the claimed mathematical result, not observed popularity.
sections.claimed_result: For an envelope Θ, divergence of ∫ₚ₀∞ Θ(p)⁻¹ dp forces uniqueness for every array in the stated class, while convergence gives a compactly supported array with two distinct Lagrangian Euler evolutions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite nondecreasing envelope Θ, p₀>2, and the paper's class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices; nonunique examples are compactly supported and evolve on [0,1].
sections.unique_caveat: The dichotomy is proved for this structured array class and envelope condition, not for arbitrary 2D Euler initial data.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of the 2D Euler Evolutions with L¹∩Lᵖ Vorticity
sections.abstract: For every prescribed 1<p<∞, the authors construct compactly supported initial vorticity in L¹(R²)∩Lᵖ(R²) with two distinct, strongly continuous Lagrangian evolutions of the unforced 2D incompressible Euler equation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed construction gives a nonuniqueness example at every finite p in the stated range and is a substantial concrete result in fluid PDE. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations and 0 influential citations; no independent expert discussion surfaced, so placement is based on the preprint's claimed result, not attention counts.
sections.claimed_result: For each p, the authors construct one datum admitting two distinct Euler evolutions that preserve vorticity exactly through their regular Lagrangian flows, with a positive-time distinction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced incompressible Euler on R² over [0,1], with compactly supported real initial vorticity in L¹∩Lᵖ; datum and construction parameters may depend on p.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an existence result for specially constructed data, not a failure of uniqueness for every datum in L¹∩Lᵖ.

sections.abstract: For d≥2, the authors give an explicit exponential upper-tail rate for a length-n self-avoiding walk reaching distance at least vn and deduce a high-probability displacement bound n/exp(c log* n).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors make a previously nonquantitative sub-ballisticity result explicit and cross-list in probability and logic; the abstract identifies proof-theoretic analysis of the earlier argument. sections.claimed_result: The authors claim exponential decay for the event that an n-step walk reaches distance vn and derive displacement at most n/exp(c log* n) with very high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Self-avoiding walk on the hypercubic lattice ℤᵈ for d≥2; c is a positive constant in the authors' stated bound.
sections.unique_caveat: The result establishes a quantitative sublinear displacement bound, not a sharp scaling exponent or scaling limit; the stated rate is weakly sublinear.

sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a global result covering the Coulomb endpoint and two boundary-condition types, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions. sections.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
sections.abstract: The authors prove a conformal scaling limit for a Boltzmann ensemble of random flat combinatorial disks and give a branching-exploration criterion intended to apply to other discrete models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper links random discrete surfaces to a continuum JT-gravity law and cross-lists probability with mathematical physics; the limit is stated in a strong local smooth-conformal topology. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations and 0 influential citations; no independent expert discussion surfaced.
sections.claimed_result: As a distinguished boundary side grows, the rescaled rectilinear-boundary Boltzmann disks converge in law to the continuum random surface described by Ferrari's path-integral formulation of flat JT gravity; the limiting conformal factor is described by a harmonic Gaussian field related to holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The proved application is the specified Boltzmann ensemble with rectilinear boundary; convergence is for conformal factors on compact interior subsets after uniformization in a fixed domain. The broader criterion requires tightness and a suitable branching exploration.
sections.unique_caveat: Generalization to other combinatorial disk models is conditional on analogous recursions and tightness; the explicit application is one ensemble and uses a conformal-welding theorem from a companion paper.
